sections.content: Sometimes the second wording does not repeat the first: it replaces it, because you said something wrong or imprecise. *Mejor dicho* ("or rather") announces that you are correcting yourself: the first part was not quite right, and the part after the marker is the right one. You know *más bien* ("rather") from B2 Unit 1, where it came after *no … sino*. It does not say that the first part was wrong; it says that the second part describes things better, so it sounds softer.

sections.title: Replacing and refining
rows: Llegamos el lunes; mejor dicho, el martes.
We arrived on Monday; or rather, on Tuesday.
Mi amiga vive en el centro; mejor dicho, cerca del centro.
My friend lives in the centre; or rather, near the centre.
No estoy enfadado; más bien estoy cansado.
I am not angry; I am rather tired.
No es un problema; más bien es una oportunidad.
It is not a problem; it is rather an opportunity.

sections.content: Use *mejor dicho* when you hear your own mistake and fix it on the spot. Use *más bien* after a negative sentence, to give the better description. Compare *es decir* from B1 Unit 27: it repeats the same idea, while *mejor dicho* changes it.
